h1: The 7 Best Toaster Ovens Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 toaster ovens under $100 scored on capacity, convection and air fry airflow, and counter footprint.
summary: The BLACK+DECKER TO3250XSBD 8-slice convection oven is the best value under $100 because its fan and extra-wide cavity handle real meals, not just toast. The Hamilton Beach Easy Reach 6-slice is the safer everyday buy with a pizza function. If you want air frying, the Easy Reach air fry and BLACK+DECKER 6-slice cover it. Small kitchens should look at the 4-slice Hamilton Beach combo.
intro: The slice count on a toaster oven box is a poor guide to what it can cook. A 6-slice oven can fit a 9 by 13 pan or it can be a tall narrow box that barely takes a 9-inch pizza, and the listing rarely says which. Buyers who count slices instead of checking the shape often end up with a heater that browns the top of dinner and leaves the middle pale.

We ranked seven ovens that all sit in the $50 to $100 bucket, so the question is what each one gives you for that money. Scoring leaned hardest on cavity usefulness, whether a convection fan or air fry mode is included, element power, and how much counter space the oven claims.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER TO3250XSBD 8-Slice Extra Wide Convection Countertop
products.verdict: Eight slices, an extra-wide cavity and a convection fan for the money.
products.description:
The TO3250XSBD is the biggest oven in this ranking, rated for eight slices, and it adds convection, a fan that moves hot air around the food. That fan is what separates real roasting from simply warming food under two elements.

It beats the Hamilton Beach Easy Reach models because a wide cavity and a fan matter more than extra preset buttons. Where the Easy Reach 6-slice ovens trade width for a pizza function, this one gives you room for a larger tray and faster, more even browning. Convection also tends to shorten cook times, which eases the heat on a summer kitchen.

Best for families who want a toaster oven to replace the full oven on weeknights. The caveat is counter space: the extra-wide body needs a generous spot, and it lacks a dedicated air fry mode.
pros: Replaces the oven for small meals
cons: Needs a lot of counter space
products.idealFor: Families who want a toaster oven to handle weeknight dinners.
products.skipIf: Your counter is small or you want a true air fry setting.

products.name: Hamilton Beach Easy Reach 6 Slice Countertop Toaster Oven
products.verdict: A 6-slice oven with a pizza function and a simple, durable feature set.
products.description:
This Hamilton Beach pairs a 6-slice cavity with a pizza function, which is the setting most buyers actually use after toast. It is the plain version of the Easy Reach line, with no fan or air fry hardware to fail.

It ranks just below the BLACK+DECKER because six slices of space and no convection means slower, less even results on thicker food. Against the Easy Reach air fry model beneath it, you give up crisping but gain a simpler control scheme and fewer moving parts. The footprint is more forgiving than the 8-slice unit, so it fits more kitchens.

Pick it if you toast, reheat and bake frozen pizza and want zero fuss. The honest caveat is that without a fan it handles wings and fries poorly, and big roasts need the full oven.
products.idealFor: Households that toast, reheat and bake frozen pizza daily.
products.skipIf: You want to air fry or cook for a crowd.

products.name: Hamilton Beach Easy Reach 6 Slice Countertop Air Fryer Toaster Oven
products.verdict: The same 6-slice Easy Reach body with an air fry mode added.
products.description:
This model keeps the 6-slice Easy Reach cavity and adds an air fry mode, which in practice means a fan and a higher airflow setting for crisping frozen fries, nuggets and wings. It is the cheapest way here to get a toaster oven and an air fryer in one footprint.

It ranks third because an air fry mode in a toaster oven is smaller in capacity than a dedicated basket machine, so batches stay modest. Compared with the plain Easy Reach it adds versatility at the same price bucket, while compared with the BLACK+DECKER 6-slice air fry oven below, the Hamilton Beach brand and Easy Reach design give it a slight edge on everyday toasting.

Best for a household that wants one appliance doing both jobs. The caveat is that crowding the rack ruins the crisp, so cook in single layers.
pros: Air fry mode in one appliance
Same simple layout as the plain model
Saves buying a separate air fryer
cons: Smaller batches than a basket fryer
products.idealFor: People who want an air fryer and toaster oven on one counter.
products.skipIf: You need to cook large air fried batches.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 6-Slice Air Fry Toaster Oven
products.verdict: A 6-slice air fry oven aimed at heavier daily use.
products.description:
BLACK+DECKER's 6-slice air fry oven covers the same ground as the Hamilton Beach air fry model, with a six-slice cavity and an air fry setting. It is positioned for busier households that run the oven several times a day.

It sits one rung below the Hamilton Beach because the two share capacity and function, and the Hamilton Beach Easy Reach design is the more proven one for reheating. This BLACK+DECKER is the better choice if you already own BLACK+DECKER small appliances or find it on sale. It trails the 8-slice convection model by a wide margin on cavity size.

Choose it for a busy kitchen where air frying is a regular habit. The caveat is that, like any six-slice oven, thick roasts and large trays will not fit.
cons: Small for roasts and big trays
Little to separate it from rivals
products.idealFor: Busy kitchens that air fry a few times a week.
products.skipIf: You want the extra-wide cavity of the 8-slice model.

products.name: Cuisinart Toaster Oven Broiler
products.verdict: A stainless 1800W oven with a broiler for browning tops.
products.description:
Cuisinart's Toaster Oven Broiler is a stainless steel 1800W unit built around fast heat and a broil element. That wattage is high for the category, which helps recover temperature each time you open the door.

It ranks below the air fry ovens because it offers no fan, so airflow is natural rather than forced, and there is no crisping setting. It beats the compact Hamilton Beach models on build and power, which is why it holds fifth. The middle-of-the-road price is fair for a stainless body that wipes clean.

Best for a cook who toasts open-faced sandwiches, melts cheese and finishes casseroles under the broiler. The caveat is that the listing gives no capacity figure, so check the interior size against your favorite pan before ordering.
cons: No air fry or convection mode
products.idealFor: Cooks who broil sandwiches, cheese and casseroles.
products.skipIf: You want crisping or a stated large capacity.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 4 Slice Countertop Air Fryer Toaster Oven Combo
products.verdict: A 4-slice air fry combo that fits tight counters.
products.description:
This Hamilton Beach shrinks the formula to a 4-slice cavity while keeping an air fry mode, which makes it the practical oven for a dorm, studio or small kitchen. It is the lowest-cost pick in the roundup.

It ranks sixth because four slices is a tight limit: a standard frozen pizza will not fit and a roasting dish will not either. Compared with the 6-slice Easy Reach air fry model above, you save counter space but give up the capacity that makes an air fry mode useful for a family-size batch.

Buy it for one or two people who air fry snacks and toast bread. The caveat is that small cavities heat quickly but crowd easily, so batches must stay small to crisp.
pros: Good for one or two people
cons: Will not fit a standard pizza
products.skipIf: You cook for three or more people.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 2-in-1 Countertop Toaster Oven and Long Slot 2 Slice
products.verdict: A toaster and a small oven in one stainless body.
products.description:
This stainless Hamilton Beach pairs a 2-slice long-slot toaster with a countertop oven, so it can toast bread and bake small items at the same time. It is the only appliance here that doubles as a true slot toaster.

It finishes last because the oven side is small, with no convection and no air fry, and the fuller feature set costs more than its capacity warrants. Against the 4-slice Hamilton Beach combo above, it trades cooking range for the convenience of a dedicated toasting slot, which suits a household that makes toast every morning.

It makes sense for someone who wants one appliance instead of two on a crowded counter. The caveat is that anything bigger than a few pieces of toast or a personal pizza belongs in another oven.
products.idealFor: Morning toast-makers short on counter space.
products.skipIf: You want to bake or air fry more than toast.

whatMatters.detail: Slice count is a rough proxy for cavity width, not volume. An eight-slice oven like the BLACK+DECKER TO3250XSBD takes larger trays than a six-slice Easy Reach. Check whether the listing states pizza or pan size, since two ovens with the same slice number can differ in depth. Measure your favorite baking dish before you buy.

A fan moves hot air across food, which browns more evenly and cooks faster. Air fry modes push that harder for crisping. The BLACK+DECKER 8-slice has convection, while the Hamilton Beach and BLACK+DECKER 6-slice models add air fry. Look for the words convection, air fry or fan on the listing; without them, you get still-air heat.

Wattage affects how fast the oven heats and recovers after the door opens. The Cuisinart lists 1800W, which is strong for the category. Higher power helps with toast speed and broiling, but wattage alone does not guarantee even results, so pair it with a fan if browning matters.

A big oven that crowds your counter ends up stored in a cabinet and unused. Compare external width and depth, plus clearance for the door and the vent. The Hamilton Beach 4-slice combo fits tight spots, while the extra-wide BLACK+DECKER needs room. Leave a few inches behind the oven for heat.

Crumbs and grease build up fast in a toaster oven. A removable crumb tray and a wipeable interior make maintenance easy, and stainless bodies like the Cuisinart resist stains. Check the listing for a crumb tray and for whether the rack and pan are dishwasher or hand-wash only.

howToChoose.intro: Match the slice count to the biggest thing you cook, not to how many pieces of toast you make.

faq.q: Can a toaster oven replace my full oven?
faq.a: For small meals, yes. The BLACK+DECKER TO3250XSBD 8-slice handles larger trays and cooks faster with convection. For big roasts or multiple dishes, the Hamilton Beach 6-slice models run out of room.

faq.q: Is an air fry toaster oven as good as a basket air fryer?
faq.a: Not quite. The Hamilton Beach Easy Reach Air Fryer and BLACK+DECKER 6-slice crisp well in single layers but hold smaller batches. A basket fryer wins on volume; these win on versatility.

faq.q: Are 6-slice ovens big enough for pizza?
faq.a: It depends on the shape. The Hamilton Beach Easy Reach 6 Slice lists a pizza function, but check the interior against your pizza size. The 8-slice BLACK+DECKER is the safer choice for larger pies.
Preheat for baking and pizza, since the cavity needs to reach temperature for browning. Toast and reheating work from cold. The Cuisinart's 1800W element heats quickly, which shortens the wait.

faq.q: How do I keep a toaster oven clean?
faq.a: Empty the crumb tray often, wipe the interior after greasy cooks, and avoid foil lining the bottom. A stainless body like the Cuisinart or Hamilton Beach 2-in-1 wipes down easily.

faq.q: Is the 2-in-1 combo worth it over a separate toaster?
faq.a: Only if counter space is tight. The Hamilton Beach 2-in-1 gives you a long slot toaster and a small oven in one body, but its oven is limited compared with the 4-slice air fry combo.

finalTake: The BLACK+DECKER TO3250XSBD 8-Slice Convection is the best use of $100 here, giving you capacity and a fan that most budget ovens skip. The Hamilton Beach Easy Reach 6 Slice is the simple, reliable alternative with a pizza function. Pick an air fry model only if you will really use it, and take the 4-slice Hamilton Beach combo when counter space is the constraint.
